name: Mongol Empire
summary: A rapidly expanding empire created by Chinggis Khan’s unification of steppe peoples, connecting large parts of Eurasia through conquest and exchange.
capital: A mobile royal court initially; Karakorum developed as an imperial capital under Ögödei in the 1230s.
economy: Pastoral resources, taxation, tribute, and long-distance trade supported imperial expansion and consumption.
military: Highly mobile mounted forces conducted successive campaigns across Eurasia; conquered populations also supplied personnel and expertise.
contributions: Expanded Eurasian travel, commerce, and exchanges of skills and knowledge, alongside extensive destruction and forced displacement.
origin: Temüjin united rival steppe groups and was proclaimed Chinggis Khan in 1206.
decline: Succession conflicts and competing dynastic interests produced civil war and the division of authority among successor khanates.

sources.title: Cambridge — The Rise of Chinggis Khan and the United Empire, 1206–1260
Royal Armouries — Rise of the Mongols
Columbia University — Collapse of the Empire

periodNote: This record uses the united empire, 1206–1260. Successor khanates and nominal claims to unity continued; 1260 is not the end of all Mongol rule.
